access.edition_or_version: Written 1979; published 1981 in Mere Dil Mere Musafir; carried into public protest by Iqbal Bano's 1986 rendition at Alhamra
access.language_used: en (English-language descriptions only; the Urdu text was not inspected)

tone_mechanisms_observed: antithesis and negation: the coming reckoning is set against present power, with the negation of existing authority as the hinge
short, end-stopped declaratives giving a collective, chant-adjacent rhythm
closing vow as anticipated vindication rather than a request
mechanics.emotional_progression: Present power named and negated, then an anticipated vindication that closes the poem without asking anything (dossier section D).
mechanics.contested_reading: Attributed reading contested: scholars such as Rauf Parekh dispute the common reading that it targeted Zia-ul-Haq, arguing it honoured the 1979 Iranian revolution (dossier section E).
mechanics.translation_limit: Urdu nazm; this dossier inspected English-language descriptions, not the Urdu text, so claims about its sound, rhyme, and register are bounded (dossier section E).
